# Amos Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 335v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/AMO_003_page_001.jpg

---

**3:1** Hear [shimu] this word [ha-davar] which YHWH has-spoken [dibber] against-you [aleikhem], O-sons of-Yisra'el, against all the-family [mishpachah] which I-brought-up [he'eleiti] from-the-land of-Mitsrayim, saying:

**3:2** "Only you [raq etkhem] I-have-known [yadati] from-all the-families [mishpechot] of-the-earth [ha-adamah]; therefore [al-ken] I-will-visit [efqod] upon-you all your-iniquities [avonotekhem]."

**3:3** "Will-two [hashelayim] walk [yelkhu] together [yachdav] unless [bilti im] they-have-agreed [no'adu]?"

**3:4** "Will-a-lion [aryeh] roar [yish'ag] in-the-forest [ba-ya'ar] when-there-is-no [ein lo] prey [terep]? Will-a-young-lion [kefir] give [yitten] his-voice [qolo] from-his-den [mi-me'onato] unless [bilti im] he-has-caught [lakhad] [something]?"

**3:5** "Will-a-bird [tsippor] fall [tippol] to-a-snare [pach] on-the-ground [ha-arets] when-there-is-no [ein] trap [moqesh] for-it? Will-a-snare spring-up [ya'aleh] from-the-ground when-it-has-not-caught [lo yilkod] anything [lakhod]?"

**3:6** "If-a-trumpet [shofar] is-blown [yittaqa] in-a-city, will-the-people [am] not tremble [lo yecheradu]? If-evil [ra'ah] befalls [tihyeh] a-city, has-not YHWH done-it [asah]?"

**3:7** "For the-Lord [Adonai] YHWH does nothing [lo ya'aseh davar] unless [ki im] he-reveals [galah] his-secret [sodo] to his-servants [avadav] the-prophets [ha-nevi'im]."

**3:8** "A-lion [aryeh] has-roared [sha'ag]; who will-not fear [lo yira]? The-Lord [Adonai] YHWH has-spoken [dibber]; who will-not prophesy [lo yinnave]?"

**3:9** "Proclaim [hashmi'u] upon the-fortresses [armonot] in-Ashdod and-upon the-fortresses in-the-land of-Mitsrayim, and-say: 'Gather [he'asefu] upon the-mountains [harei] of-Shomron [Samaria], and-see [ur'u] great [rabbот] tumults [mehumot] in-her-midst [betokah], and-the-oppressed [ashuqim] in-her-midst.'"

**3:10** "And-they-do-not know [lo yade'u] [how] to-do right [nekhochah]," declares YHWH, "those-who-store-up [ha-otserim] violence [chamas] and-destruction [shod] in-their-fortresses."

**3:11** Therefore, thus says the-Lord YHWH: "An-adversary [tsar], and-surrounding [u-seviv] the-land, and-he-will-bring-down [vehorid] from-you your-strength [uzzekh], and-your-fortresses will-be-plundered [venavazszu]."

**3:12** Thus says YHWH: "As the-shepherd [ha-ro'eh] rescues [yatstsil] from-the-mouth [mi-pi] of-the-lion two [shtei] legs [khera'ayim] or-a-piece [bedal] of-an-ear [ozen], so will-be-rescued [yinnatzslu] the-sons of-Yisra'el, those-who-sit [ha-yoshvim] in-Shomron on-the-corner [bi-fe'at] of-a-couch [mittah] and-on-the-damask [bi-demesheq] of-a-bed [ares]."

**3:13** "Hear [shimu] and-testify [veha'idu] against-the-house of-Yaakov," declares the-Lord YHWH, the-God of-Hosts [Elohei Tseva'ot]:

**3:14** "For on-the-day [be-yom] I-visit [poqdi] the-transgressions [pish'ei] of-Yisra'el upon-him, I-will-visit [ufaqadeti] upon the-altars [mizbechot] of-Beit-El [Bethel], and-the-horns [qarnot] of-the-altar will-be-cut-off [venighde'u] and-fall [venaflu] to-the-ground [la-arets]."

**3:15** "And-I-will-strike [vehikkeiti] the-winter-house [beit ha-choref] together-with [al] the-summer-house [beit ha-qayits]; and-the-houses of-ivory [ha-shen] will-perish [ve'avdu], and-many [rabbim] houses will-come-to-an-end [vesafu]," declares YHWH.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — "Only you have I known":** *Yadati* ("known") — intimate knowledge, as in election/covenant. The logic is staggering: *because* Israel is chosen, they face *greater* accountability. Election intensifies judgment, not exempts from it.

**v.3-6 — The cause-and-effect questions:** Seven rhetorical questions, each establishing that effects have causes. The series culminates in v.6b: "If calamity comes to a city, has not YHWH caused it?" This is not abstract theology — it is the theological foundation for what follows.

**v.12 — "Two legs or a piece of an ear":** The shepherd produces the remnants to prove to the flock's owner that the animal was indeed killed by a predator (cf. Exodus 22:13). The "rescue" is ironic — all that survives of Israel will be scraps.

*— EMET*
